messages.subject: Re: Missing features error
messages.body_plain:
Dear Brett,

yes, MSstats requires that the input data file has one row for all the possible combinations of feature and run. If a peak is missing, the input data file still has to have this row, with the intensity denoted as 'NA'. We chose to ask the user to provide this information (an alternative is to guess this automatically, but the guessing is too error-prone). The text following '***' in the error message points out the peptides and the runs that do not have the row. You have two options: (1) add the rows and indicate the missing value as 'NA', or (2) remove from the dataset the feature where too many intensities are missing.

For more information please see the user manual at http://www.msstats.org/workflows.html

Hope this helps
Olga Vitek

messages.subject: Re: Missing features error
messages.body_plain:
>From the full dataset that you just sent, it looks like you have 11 distinct file names (i.e. 11 runs), but each combination of protein name, peptide sequence and precursor charge is only present 3 times.

MSstats expect each feature to be present in all the runs where any information on the protein is collected. E.g., if a protein has at least one relevant intensity in 11 runs, then each feature has to have 11 rows, with 'NA' when missing. If you did a targeted experiment and split the proteins across different 'methods' (e.g. intensities of a protein were acquired in 6 runs, but were never present in the remaining 5 runs), then each feature of the protein has to have 6 rows, with 'NA' when missing.

messages.subject: Re: Missing features error
messages.body_plain:
Dear Brett,

Thank you for sharing error message and subset of your data.
Now I found where this issue came from. Proteins in this dataset has same name of peptide (as you asked me before). When MSstats checkes the missingness in dataProcess step, it uses unique feature name (combination of peptide and transition. here protein names is not included.) therefore, MSstats give you some error message. So, here is the solution. If you use direct R,

raw<-read.csv("sample.data.csv")

raw$PeptideSequence<-paste(raw$ProteinName, raw$PeptideSequence,sep="_") ## make unique peptide name across proteins

quant<-dataProcess(raw)

We will update this issue in MSstats.daily and external tool in Skyline soon, then you don't need to worry about the same peptide name in different proteins.

Thank you again!

messages.subject: Re: Missing features error
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Brett.

First of all, this is not an error message, but just summary of NAs in data. '# transitions are completely missing in one condition'  shows that some transitions have all NAs in certain condition. You can check it in data itself. For example, please check protein=sp|Q3TCH7|CUL4A_MOUSE, peptide=RPNKPAELIAK, precursorcharge=3, fragmention=precursor [M+2], product charge=3, and either healthy or disease has all NAs or not. You also can check with profile plot in dataProcessPlots, disconnected lines means missing values (NAs in 'intensity' column).

The reason that we show this summary is to give the user some idea about count of NAs. then Users can go back to software they used (Skyline or anything else), then double check the process from software. Sometimes, it could be small mistakes, such as transition is not selected, or some subject is not selected or some problem to process. or  it can be meaningful missingness. Therefore, we hope that users know about this issues of data and decide about missingness before running further analysis. Another reason is that the missingness can affect to analyze the data in MSstats. If there is complete missingness of certain condition for some features, MSstats will use additive model (no interaction term). If there is complete missingness of certain condition for all features, MSstats can not do groupComparision.
Therefore, you can go ahead further analysis. Visualization from dataProcessPlots and groupComparison and so on.

And We will try to be clear about previous message (actual error message which is not complete output from peak processing software) and this message (summary of missingness which can affect further analysis).

Thank you!

Meena

messages.subject: Re: p value and adjusted p value
messages.subject_clean: p value and adjusted p value
messages.body_plain: Adjusted p-values control for the multiplicity of testing. Since we fit a separate model, and conduct a separate comparison for each protein, the number of tests equals the number of comparisons. A 0.05 cutoff of an adjusted p-value controls the False Discovery Rate in the collection of tests over all the proteins at 5%. Since they account for the multiplicity, adjusted p-values are more conservative (i.e. it is more difficult to detect a change). The p-values are adjusted by the method of Benhamini and Hochberg, and are sometimes referred to as q-values. All this is for the quantitative comparison only, and is completely unrelated to the FDR, q-values etc reported for identification (e.g. with database search in DDA experiments).

messages.subject: Re: p value and adjusted p value
messages.subject_clean: p value and adjusted p value
messages.body_plain:
Dear Diego,

'pvalue' column is calculated by Tvalue (test statistics : calculated by log fold change and standard error) and DF(degree of freedom). and adjusted p-value means that the 'pvalue' column are adjusted for comparisons across multiple proteins using the approach by Benjamini and Hochberg. (there is reference in p21 of MSstats.daily 2.1.5 user manual at workflow webpage.)

about zero value in p value : this is not normal. Yes, this is approximation problem. when pvalue is equal to 0, this means really close to 0.

I hope it will be helpful for you.

Meena

messages.subject: FAQ : Peptide-level analysis
messages.body_plain:
We got several emails about peptide level analysis instead of protein level.
It is quite simple, with just one modification. If you want to significance analysis on peptides, please use peptide names in 'ProteinName' column of input data. (Because significance analysis will be performed by unique names of 'ProteinName' column) For example,

ProteinName     PeptideSequence
Peptide1              Peptide1
Peptide1              Peptide1
Peptide2              Peptide2
Peptide2              Peptide2

I hope that it will be helpful for users.

Meena

> a) open R

messages.subject: MSstats.daily v2.1.6 release!
messages.body_plain:
MSstats.daily v2.1.6 is released on 'INSTALLATION' page of msstats.org <http://msstats.org/> on March 19, 2014.

1. dataProcess function
1) Added a more explicit warnings for handling missing peaks. MSstats input requires NAs for missing peaks. New warning messages will say whether there is no information (no rows) for missing peaks or duplicate of measurements. For label-based experiments, warning messages will say whether missing rows come from reference peptides or endogenous peptides, also whether there are some peptides completely missing features across all runs, in which case users need to check the processing in spectral processing tools. (Thanks, Jantine)

2) Added new option addMissingRows.  If addMissingRows=TRUE, list of missing feature will be reported, missing rows for missing peaks will be added with intensity=NA and then input will be ready to further analysis. This will be helpful especially for DDA data which is generated by spectral processing tools that doesn't produce NAs for missing peaks. (Thanks, Brett)

3) Fixed the bug for assigning the option of nameStandards when normalization="globalStandards" (Thanks, Tobias)

4) PeptideModifiedSequence column is also accepted instead of PeptideSequence column in MSstats required input. If there are some peptides who are present in a modified and unmodified form, PeptideModifiedSequence column from Skyline is suitable for analysis. MSstats report from MSstats external tool in Skyline includes PeptideModifiedSequence column instead of PeptideSequence column. (Thanks, Tobias)

2. Fixed minor bugs in designSampleSize and quantification functions.

MSstats external tool v2.1.6 in Skyline will be released in a couple of days.
Welcome to hear your feedback!

Meena

messages.subject: Re: Analysis of DIA (SWATH-MS) data processed by different software tools
messages.subject_clean: Analysis of DIA (SWATH-MS) data processed by different software tools
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tobias,

You are doing this correctly. If the signal processing groups all the fragments, then the data structure is the same as in label-free DDA and technically it can be analyzed as such.

The real question is whether this is a good thing to do. On one hand, by combining multiple fragments into a single feature we lose information (e.g. if one of the fragments is poor quality, it affects the entire feature). On the other hand, if the combination of the fragments into a feature is done in an intelligent way (e.g. only keeping good-quality features, consistently keeping the same fragments across all the runs to avoid bias, and eliminating missing values) then this can potentially be a good thing.

Of course the users may not have much choice in this, but it is possible to use multiple spectral processing tools and compare. Would it be possible for you to share with us your results, at least at a very high and non-detailed level? It will be interesting to know which approach was beneficial.

Best wishes
Olga Vitek
